w: Prior to his morning puja, Swamishri performed the pratishtha rituals for the new Hari mandir in Ganad, Surendranagar district.

In the evening a dedication assembly was held for the 18 earthquake-hit schools built by BAPS. Through the inspiration of Swamishri the BAPS has undertaken the reconstruction of 8 earthquake-hit villages (4 of which have been built and inaugurated), 43 Primary schools, 6 Secondary schools and a colony in Bhuj. The 18 schools (15 primary schools and 3 secondary schools) by Swamishri were dedicated to each principal and leading figure of every village. The Honorable State Minister, Shri I. K. Jadeja and Shri Fakirbhai Vaghela spoke laudingly of the Sanstha's earthquake rehabilitation projects. More than 5,000 people attended the dedication assembly. (For details see NEWS report) Note: Names of 18 schools built aew as follows:
Bhadreshi Ganjela
Malod Mansar
Bakarthali Tikar
Vana Mojidad
Khodu Chhalala
Dedadra Pandri
Limli Acharda
Bhadiyad Sejakpar

st.t: January-2001-Gujarat Earthquaqke 2001, BAPS Earthquake Victims Rehabilitation Project - Pramukh Swami Maharaj dedicates 18 schools 17 May 2002, Surendranagar
w: With the blessings and guidance of Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) is currently active in a wide range of earthquake rehabilitation services. On 17 May 2002, in Gujarat, a special dedication assembly was held in Surendranagar, in which 18 schools reconstructed by BAPS were presented to the people by Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Over 8,000 people attended the assembly in which Swamishri presented the name plaques of the reconstructed schools to the school and village officials. Then 4 of the 18 school principals addressed the assembly. They said that on their request Pramukh Swami Maharaj agreed to reconstruct their schools without a moment’s delay. On this occasion one of the honourable guests, State Minister Shri I.K. Jadeja, said, “The district of Surendranagar is very fortunate since Pramukh Swami Maharaj, who is revered worldwide and inspires noble values in people throughout the world, has presented these schools which will be centres for value-based education. Now it is necessary for the people of Surendranagar to use these schools to provide value-based education.” State Minister Shri Fakirbhai Vaghela said, “First I thank Pramukh Swami Maharaj for reconstructing 18 schools for this district. It seems that he has resolved our difficulties to provide us with opportunities. Swamishri’s sadhus are highly educated. Many are from England and America. That such sadhus have renounced the world and are engaged in this earthquake relief work to serve us is no ordinary matter. I have seen many of the Sanstha’s mandirs, met many of the sadhus and know Swamiji personally. That is why I say that these schools will be centres for learning values.” Blessing the assembly, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, “God is very merciful. From Him we learn to be compassionate and due to His grace this work is possible.” Swamishri especially thanked the donors and blessed that they be able to continue to support such noble work. He also thanked the villagers, officials and contractors who helped in the reconstruction. Also, Swamishri blessed, “May the children who study here also gain noble virtues, pride for their country, become ideal citizens and increase the prestige of our state and country. May they keep dharma and God at the forefront in all their work. Just like Arjun had kept the strength of God at the forefront and won, may the students all become like Arjun.” Also present on this occasion were the local MLA Shri Dhanraj Kela, the District Collector, and representatives of the donors, namely, Deputy General Manager of Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) and others.

ds.t: Every moment in seva and devotion!
w: Today there was a check-up of Pramukh Swami Maharaj's health. Dr Mamtora and Dr Mahendrabhai examined Swamishri. Dr Mahendrabhai measured Swamishri's blood pressure. It was 100 over 62 at that time and the pulse was 58. After taking a tablet with a little water, Swamishri remained busy reading letters. At 8.45 am Swamishri was to leave for the hospital.
Seated in Dhirubhai's car, Swamishri set off for the hospital. A little while had passed when Swamishri asked, "Are there letters to be read?"
"Yes."
"Bring them." Putting on his glasses, Swamishri became busy reading letters.

Swamishri was taken straight to the room for the angiography. While other preparations were being made, Swamishri's attention was not on those arrangements. Swamishri was busy arranging for Harikrishna Maharaj, whom he had brought with him: where shall we keep Thakorji? He himself said, "Keep Him in a corner on the left where I can have darshan." When the attendants had completed the arrangement, the doctors seated Swamishri on the movable stretcher of the CT scan.
Every moment of Swamishri is filled with seva and devotion, whatever the condition of the body!

The BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir has been built of pink stone from Rajasthan in the Nagradi style. It is 80 ft high, 169 ft long and 128 ft wide. The mandir has five shikhars, one main dome, five small and six large domes; 136 ornate arches (torans), 136 carved pillars, 20 gavakshs, 21 jharukhas, 61 murtis on the mandir pillars, 40 murtis in the mandovar, 24 murtis inside the ghummats.

From 8.00 am the prasad pravesh rituals, prior to the pratishtha day, were held in the presence of senior sadhus. Swamishri came and performed the pujan of kalashes and dhaja-dand and the concluding rituals of prasad pravesh. At 7.00 pm Swamishri saw a drama presentation of how Satsang has developed in Bhavnagar. The drama included the stories of Brahmanand Swami’s transformation, Sagram Vaghri of Limli, Atmaram Darji, Bhakta Kuberbhai who begged for alms with Shastriji Maharaj, and incidents on how Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj had developed the Satsang. The drama concluded at 8.20 pm.

The Home Minister of Uganda, Dr Rugunda visited Swamishri. He had been impressed on seeing Swaminarayan Akshardham during his recent visit to New Delhi. He told Swamishri that it was wonderful and there was no doubt that it is one of the wonders of the world. He asked Swamishri to bless his country with peace and prosperity. Swamishri assured him that he would pray daily.

In the evening welcome assembly at the mandir Viveksagar Swami addressed the gathering. Thereafter the youths performed a welcome dance for Swamishri and also presented a drama on Hira Mukhi. Swamishri was then garlanded by senior sadhus and leading devotees. Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly, “Satsang in Kampala has existed since the time of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Through their wish and grace the mandir was built here. Due to certain circumstances a difficulty arose some time ago but by God’s wish and the blessings of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj peace returned to the country. The new government handed over all the mandirs to their respective followers. Due to our true bhakti God inspired all and we too received our mandir back and today all of us are doing bhajan and bhakti here. Through inner faith and trust one’s mission is realized.”

For the convenience of devotees, today’s evening satsang assembly was dedicated to celebrating Yogiji Maharaj’s birthday. During this symbolic celebration, sadhus initiated by Yogiji Maharaj, namely, Premprakash Swami, Viveksagar Swami and Kothari Swami, recollected their experiences about Yogiji Maharaj. This was followed by a video show on Yogiji Maharaj. Finally, Swamishri blessed the devotees, “Yogiji Maharaj was a divine person. One would always find him smiling, showering love and compassion, and brimming with joy. By remembering him our miseries and pains disappear.” In conclusion Swamishri was honoured with garlands by senior sadhus.

During the meetings, Bhimjibhai came from Mumbai. Seeing Bhimjibhai, originally of the village of Bhadra, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "He and that Valji (Dharmatanay Swami), these two are at the root. Before Yogiji Maharaj came to perform the installation, a pipeline had to be laid, and these two did a great deal of seva then."

After the meal, Pramukh Swami Maharaj remained busy in meetings. In particular, many devotees from India and abroad were to come to the Gunatit sthan (holy place of Gunatitanand Swami) at Bhadra to take part. Only a limited number of devotees could be seated for the installation. Among them, Swamishri was especially concerned about the Pujara family, and particularly the members of Dajibapu's family, the villagers of Bhadra and others. Swamishri had given a sadhu the seva of arranging who was to be seated where under the dome of the mandir during the installation rites. Today too Swamishri called that sadhu and, with a plan of the mandir dome, looked in detail and in depth at the arrangements he had made for who would sit where. Swamishri carefully looked at the arrangements for Chandrakantbhai Pujara, Kumarbhai Pujara and their family, for Nirmalsinh Rana and about 25 members of his family from Dajibapu's family, for Mansukhbhai Bhanderi of the village who lives in America, and for the devotees and leaders of the village.

After discussing these arrangements, Swamishri sat in a meeting with Dharmakunvar Swami, Gnanprasad Swami and Narayanmuni Swami. In the time of Yogiji Maharaj, when the pran pratishtha was first done here in a single spired mandir, Ghanshyamsinh Bapu had wished that flower petals be showered by helicopter. This time, the wish to shower flowers during the installation had been made by Mansukh Bhanderi, originally from this village and now living in America. Swamishri discussed this matter every day. Today too Swamishri took up this matter for discussion. Tirthswarup Swami of Mumbai was arranging the helicopter. At first there was talk of landing this helicopter at Dhrol, but Swamishri instructed that a helipad be made in Bhadra itself instead of Dhrol. Swamishri also took a deep interest in who would sit in the helicopter during the shower of flowers.
Swamishri said, "Mansukh should be seated."
A sadhu said, "He does not wish to."

Swamishri said, "No, he should specially be seated. His son should also be seated, and since it was Ghanshyamsinh Bapu's wish, Hitendrasinh, the son of Shambhusinh from that family, should also be seated. Along with them, also have a videographer."
Swamishri also instructed that the people of the village be invited for meals during the festival.
Swamishri is the divine navigator of the human mind.

During the meetings, Bhimjibhai came from Mumbai. Seeing Bhimjibhai, who is originally from the village of Bhadra, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "He and that Valji (Dharmatanay Swami), these two are at the root. Before Yogiji Maharaj came to perform the installation, a pipeline had to be laid, and these two did great seva then."
